newsitem.title: UK: SBC Warburg cuts European interest rate forecasts.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg cuts European interest rate forecasts.

text.p: SBC Warburg said on Wednesday it had lowered its interest rate forecasts for Europe and expected to see a further 50 basis points cut in German short term interest rates over the next three months.
"The rationale for a German rate cut is not domestic conditions but rather mounting pressure for lower rates in Europe," analysts in SBC Warburg's macroeconomic group said in a statement.

They said domestic demand growth in France was forecast to slow down in 1997 and this weaker growth could lead to France having greater difficulties in meeting the fiscal criteria of the Maastricht Treaty.
The French inflation outlook was positive, the analysts said, setting a forecast of 1.3 percent inflation next year with risks to the downside.

For Germany, the economic outlook was more promising for 1997 and while on domestic grounds Germany could probably leave monetary policy unchanged for the next 12 months, a rate cut would not jeopardise the inflation outlook, they said.
"However with EMU still firmly on the agenda, the Bundesbank needs to provide more monetary stimulus to the rest of Europe. We expect Buba to fulfill its new obligations," they said.
At the same time SBC Warburg raised its forecasts for dollar/mark, dollar rates against European currencies generally and sterling/mark.
